subject: SIG kickoff and clarifying questions for HelixHealth
body:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Lila Morgan <lila.morgan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: SIG kickoff and clarifying questions for HelixHealth

Hi Lila — great running through the integration requirements earlier. Per our call, we want to kick off the vendor security questionnaire and make sure we scope the right forms (SIG vs CAIQ vs custom). I attached a prefilled SIG template that covers usual items — feel free to mark where you prefer us to provide evidence vs where you'd prefer your team to validate.

A few clarifying Qs to help our security team pick the right path and evidence set:
- Compliance scope: do you need Redwood to attest on SOC 2 Type II, or is SOC 2 Type I acceptable for initial procurement?
- Regulated data: will the integration surface PHI (HIPAA) or special category personal data (GDPR) in production? If PHI, are you expecting a BAA?
- Deployment: are you onboarding to HelixHealth's VPC (private connectivity) or will you use public-hosted endpoints? (This affects evidence we provide for network controls.)
- Authentication: do you expect mutual TLS, API keys, or SSO enterprise SAML/OIDC for production integration?
- Timeline: when does procurement need the completed questionnaire / evidence?

Next steps I propose: I) you confirm SOC 2/PHI expectations and timeline, II) we exchange security contact vCard for evidence sharing, III) security (Hannah) will follow with a short technical checklist if PHI is in scope.

Attachments: redwood_sig_prefill_v1.xlsx (prefill, ticks on common items).

Thanks — we’ll keep this tight so you can get it to procurement quickly.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

> 
> - SOC 2: Procurement requires SOC 2 Type II for enterprise contracts, but for our pilot a SOC 2 Type I + active remediation plan is acceptable.
> - PHI: Yes, we will be sending limited PHI (patient identifiers + scheduling metadata) to your API during the pilot. We will need a BAA executed before production.
> - Deployment: Pilot will use public endpoints behind our gateway (no VPC peering initially).
> - Auth: API keys for pilot; production will move to mutual TLS and SSO where possible.
> - Timeline: Procurement wants a completed questionnaire and evidence package in ~3 weeks (target: 06/07/2027).

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lila Morgan <lila.morgan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG kickoff and clarifying questions for HelixHealth

Hi Lila — Hannah from Security here. Thanks for the quick clarifications. A few technical follow-ups so we can assemble evidence and scope the BAA correctly: 

1) PHI details: can you confirm which specific identifiers you will send in the pilot (e.g., full MRN, name, DOB, or pseudonymized IDs)? Will any attachments (documents/images) contain PHI?
2) Data retention: what is your expected retention window for data stored by Redwood during the pilot (days/weeks)?
3) Encryption: we encrypt in transit (TLS 1.2+ by default) and at rest (AES-256). Do you require FIPS-validated modules or HSM-backed key storage for the pilot/production?
4) Access control: who on your side will need admin-level access to logs or support sessions? Please provide names/emails so we can include them in access control evidence (or we can provide RBAC screenshots).
5) Network: since pilot uses public endpoints, will you require IP allowlisting on our side, or will you secure with API key + gateway controls?

If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-minute call with you and your security engineer to walk the SIG prefill together. I can also annotate the prefilled spreadsheet and flag items we will own vs items you need to validate.

Thanks — I’ll hold off assembling SOC evidence until we confirm the PHI shape and retention.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

On Tue, 18 May 2027 at 08:42:05 -0700, Lila Morgan <lila.morgan@helixhealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Hannah — thanks. Answers inline below: 
> 
> 1) PHI: Pilot will send pseudonymized patient ID + DOB and appointment timestamps. No images or attachments with PHI in the pilot. We will not send full names or MRNs for the initial phase.
> 2) Retention: 30 days for pilot logs and payloads, with deletion request after 30 days. Production retention will be negotiated, ~365 days likely.
> 3) Encryption: Pilot does not require FIPS or HSM; production may require HSM-backed keys (TBD).
> 4) Access: I'll add two people for admin access: Marcus Chen (marcus.chen@helixhealth.com) and Priya Desai (priya.desai@helixhealth.com). They can be included in evidence screenshots.
> 5) Network: We prefer API key + gateway controls for the pilot. We may move to IP allowlisting in production.
> 
> We can do a 20-minute sync Wed afternoon; I’ll let you know which time works.
> 
> Best,
> Lila

Thanks Lila/Hannah — this is great. Quick recap and next steps high level: 

- Scope: Pilot requires SOC 2 Type I + BAA; procurement expects Type II for enterprise (we will note this and provide roadmap).
- PHI shape: pseudonymized IDs + DOB + timestamps; no attachments. Redwood security will prepare a tailored evidence packet for the pilot (30-day retention) and hold off on SOC artifacts until pilot is signed.
- Auth/Network: pilot = API key + gateway; production = mTLS/SSO + optional IP allowlisting.
- Timeline: target questionnaire + evidence to Helix security by 2027-06-07 per procurement target.

Action items:
- Avery: upload annotated SIG prefill to the shared Drive folder and notify procurement (HubSpot deal linked) — DONE (link below).
- Hannah: assemble pilot evidence (encryption screenshots, RBAC, retention policy excerpt) and prepare to deliver to security@helixhealth.com.
- Lila: confirm Wed availability for a 20-minute sync so we can walk the prefill together.

Thanks all — looking forward to locking the pilot in.
